TSP.description: Traveling Salesman Problem - find shortest route visiting all cities exactly once and returning to start

methods.name: Nearest Neighbor
steps: Choose a random starting city
Select the closest unvisited city
Repeat until all cities are visited
Return to the starting city
methods.best_for: small-scale problems or rough estimates
methods.limitations: may not find the optimal solution

methods.name: 2-Opt
steps: Generate an initial random route
Select two random edges and reverse the path between them
Check if the new route is shorter
Repeat until no improvements are found
methods.best_for: improving existing solutions
methods.limitations: may get stuck in local optima

methods.name: Christofides Algorithm
steps: Create a minimum spanning tree of the cities
Find a minimum-weight perfect matching of the odd-degree vertices
Combine the tree and the matching to form a multigraph
Find an Eulerian circuit in the multigraph
Convert the circuit to a Hamiltonian cycle
methods.best_for: finding good approximate solutions
methods.limitations: guarantees a solution within 1.5 times the optimal, but can be slow

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm
steps: Initialize a population of random routes
Evaluate the fitness of each route
Select parents using a selection method
Perform crossover and mutation to generate new routes
Replace the least fit routes with the new ones
methods.best_for: large-scale problems with complex constraints
methods.limitations: computationally intensive and may not converge

methods.name: Ant Colony Optimization
steps: Initialize a set of artificial ants
Each ant traverses the cities and deposits pheromone trails
Evaluate the fitness of each ant's route
Update the pheromone trails based on the fitness
Repeat until convergence
methods.best_for: dynamic or distributed TSP instances
methods.limitations: can be sensitive to parameter settings

methods.name: Branch and Bound
steps: Create a tree of partial routes
Evaluate the lower bound of each node
Prune branches that cannot lead to an optimal solution
Explore the remaining branches
Return the optimal solution found
methods.best_for: small- to medium-scale problems
methods.limitations: can be slow for large instances

methods.name: Greedy Algorithm
steps: Choose a random starting city
At each step, choose the city that improves the route the most
Continue until all cities visited
methods.best_for: small instances or rough estimate
methods.limitations: may not find optimal solution

methods.name: Brute Force
steps: Generate all possible routes
Evaluate each route
Choose the shortest route
methods.best_for: very small instances
methods.limitations: computationally infeasible for large instances

methods.name: Annealing
steps: Start with a random initial solution
Simulate a Boltzmann process to gradually converge to a good solution
Re-anneal until a desired temperature is reached
methods.best_for: large instances where good approximation sufficient
methods.limitations: can get stuck in local optima

methods.name: Brute-force
steps: Generate all possible permutations of cities
Calculate total distance for each permutation
Select the permutation with the shortest distance
methods.best_for: Small instances with up to 10 cities
methods.limitations: Exponential time complexity (factorial growth)

methods.name: Dynamic Programming (Held-Karp)
steps: Compute minimum path costs for subsets of cities using recurrence relations
Store partial solutions in a memoization table
Reconstruct the shortest path from stored results
methods.best_for: Medium instances with up to 20-30 cities
methods.limitations: High memory requirement (O(n²2^n))

methods.name: Nearest Neighbor Heuristic
steps: Start at a random city
At each step, visit the nearest unvisited city
Repeat until all cities are visited and return to start
methods.best_for: Quick approximate solutions for large problems
methods.limitations: Significantly suboptimal results

methods.name: Genetic Algorithms
steps: Initialize a population of random tours
Evaluate fitness (tour length) of each solution
Apply crossover, mutation, and selection iteratively
methods.best_for: Large-scale instances with acceptable near-optimality
methods.limitations: Parameter tuning and long computation time

methods.name: Simulated Annealing
steps: Start with a random tour and high temperature
Randomly perturb the current solution
Accept worse solutions probabilistically based on decreasing temperature
methods.best_for: Escaping local optima in large problems
methods.limitations: Sensitive to cooling schedule parameters

methods.name: Tabu Search
steps: Initialize a starting solution and tabu list
Generate neighboring solutions by swapping cities
Select the best non-tabu move and update the tabu list
methods.best_for: Medium to large problems with good quality heuristics
methods.limitations: Requires careful design of neighborhood and tabu criteria

VRP.description: Vehicle Routing Problem - route multiple vehicles from a depot to serve all customers optimally

methods.name: Christofides Algorithm
steps: Create a minimum spanning tree of the customers
Create a perfect matching of the odd-degree vertices
Combine the matching and the tree to create an Eulerian graph
Find an Eulerian tour in the graph
methods.best_for: small to medium-sized instances
methods.limitations: computationally expensive for large instances

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm
steps: Initialize a population of random routes
Evaluate the fitness of each route
Select routes for crossover and mutation
Replace the least fit routes with new ones
methods.best_for: large and complex instances
methods.limitations: may get stuck in local optima

methods.name: Ant Colony Optimization
steps: Initialize a set of artificial ants
Each ant constructs a route by iteratively choosing the next customer
Update the pheromone trails based on the quality of the routes
Repeat until convergence
methods.best_for: dynamic and stochastic instances
methods.limitations: computationally expensive and sensitive to parameters

methods.name: Simulated Annealing
steps: Initialize a random route
Evaluate the cost of the route
Generate a new route by applying a perturbation
Accept or reject the new route based on the Metropolis criterion
methods.best_for: instances with multiple local optima
methods.limitations: may require careful tuning of parameters

methods.name: Vehicle Routing using Google OR-Tools
steps: Define the routing model
Specify the vehicles and their capacities
Add the customers and their demands
Solve the routing problem
methods.best_for: practical and real-world instances
methods.limitations: requires familiarity with the OR-Tools library

methods.name: Breadth-First Search
steps: Initialize solution pool with depot and customer nodes
Explore all immediate neighbors
Select best neighbor solution based on vehicle capacity and distance
methods.best_for: Medium to large-sized problems with limited constraints
methods.limitations: May not find optimal solution

methods.name: 2-Opt
steps: Start with initial random solution
Iteratively remove and reinsert edges to improve route
Continue until no further improvements
methods.best_for: Small to medium-sized problems with few constraints
methods.limitations: May get stuck in local optima

methods.name: Cluster First-Routing Second (CFS)
steps: Group customers by similarity into clusters
Assign each cluster to closest vehicle
Improve routes using routing algorithms like 2-Opt
methods.best_for: Large-scale problems with many similar customers
methods.limitations: Cluster definition can be complex

methods.name: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO)
steps: Initialize pheromone trails with equal value
Iteratively select solution based on pheromone trails
Update pheromone trails based on solution quality
methods.best_for: Large and complex problems with many constraints
methods.limitations: High computational complexity and pheromone convergence issues

methods.name: VNS (Variable Neighborhood Search)
steps: Start with initial solution and neighborhood definition
Iteratively move to new neighborhood solutions
Select best solution and repeat until convergence
methods.best_for: Medium to large-sized problems with few constraints
methods.limitations: Dependent on effective neighborhood definition

methods.name: Column Generation
steps: Formulate LP-relaxation of VRP problem
Generate columns as integer solutions
Improve lower bound using linear programming and column generation
methods.best_for: Large and complex problems with many constraints
methods.limitations: High computational complexity and difficult to solve

methods.name: Solver based on Constraint Programming
steps: Model problem as constraints (e.g., capacity, routing requirements)
Solve using CP tools (e.g., Choco, Google OR-Tools)
Post-processing to satisfy additional constraints
methods.best_for: Large and complex problems with many constraints
methods.limitations: Computational intensive and may not guarantee optimality

methods.name: Mixed Integer Programming Solver
steps: Model problem as MIP formulation (e.g., branch-and-bound)
Solve using MIP solvers (e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi)
Retrieve optimal solution and analyze solution quality
methods.best_for: Medium to large-sized problems with few or many constraints
methods.limitations: Computational intensive and may not always find optimal solution

methods.name: Branch and Cut
steps: Formulate the VRP as an integer linear program
Add cutting planes to eliminate fractional solutions
Perform branch and bound to find optimal routes
methods.best_for: Small to medium-sized VRP with strict optimality requirements
methods.limitations: High computational cost for large problem instances

methods.name: Clarke-Wright Savings Algorithm
steps: Calculate savings between all customer pairs
Sort savings in descending order
Iteratively merge feasible routes using highest savings
methods.best_for: VRP with vehicle capacity constraints and moderate customer counts
methods.limitations: Greedy approach may produce suboptimal solutions

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm (GA)
steps: Initialize a population of random route combinations
Select parents based on fitness (e.g., route cost)
Apply crossover/mutation to generate new offspring
Iterate until convergence
methods.best_for: Complex VRP with multiple constraints and large-scale instances
methods.limitations: Requires tuning of parameters and may converge to local optima

methods.name: Tabu Search
steps: Generate an initial solution
Explore neighboring solutions while avoiding tabu moves
Update the tabu list based on recent changes
Iterate until stopping criteria are met
methods.best_for: VRP requiring escape from local optima
methods.limitations: Performance depends on effective tabu list management

JSP.description: Job Scheduling Problem - schedule jobs on machines to minimize total completion time or makespan

methods.name: Johnson's Algorithm
steps: Sort jobs by processing time
Schedule the shortest job first on the machine with the earliest end time
Repeat until all jobs are scheduled
methods.best_for: Two-machine problem with consistent processing times
methods.limitations: Limited to two machines

methods.name: NEH (Nawaz-Enscore-Ham) Algorithm
steps: Calculate total processing time for each job
Sort jobs in descending order of total processing time
Schedule the first two jobs and calculate the makespan
Iteratively insert the remaining jobs to minimize makespan
methods.best_for: Flow shop scheduling with multiple machines
methods.limitations: High computational complexity for large problem sizes

methods.name: CDS (Campbell-Dudek--Smith) Algorithm
steps: Calculate the total processing time for each job
Sort jobs in descending order of total processing time
Schedule the jobs on the machine with the earliest end time
Update the machine end times after each job scheduling
methods.best_for: Flow shop scheduling with multiple machines and consistent processing times
methods.limitations: May not produce optimal solutions for large problem sizes

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm
steps: Generate an initial population of random schedules
Calculate the makespan for each schedule
Select the fittest schedules and apply crossover and mutation
Repeat until a stopping criterion is met
methods.best_for: Complex job scheduling problems with multiple machines and constraints
methods.limitations: High computational complexity and may converge to local optima

methods.name: First-Come-First-Served (FCFS)
steps: Sort jobs in arrival order
Assign each job to the first available machine
Process jobs on each machine in order
methods.best_for: Simplest implementation, low computational complexity
methods.limitations: Does not minimize makespan

methods.name: Shortest Processing Time (SPT)
steps: Sort jobs by processing time
Assign each job to the machine with the shortest current total processing time
Process jobs on each machine in order
methods.best_for: Reduces makespan, suitable for online scheduling
methods.limitations: Does not consider job release times, arrival times, or machine availability

methods.name: Shortest Job First (SJF)
steps: Sort jobs by processing time
Assign each job to the machine with the shortest current job processing time
Process jobs on each machine in order
methods.best_for: Reduces makespan, suitable for systems with multiple machines
methods.limitations: Does not consider machine availability or job priorities

methods.name: Rate Monotonic Scheduling (RMS)
steps: Assign a deadline to each job
Prioritize jobs based on their deadlines
Assign each job to the first available machine
methods.best_for: Suitable for real-time systems, meets deadlines
methods.limitations: Does not minimize makespan or consider job processing times

methods.name: Least Work Remaining (LWR)
steps: Sort jobs by their remaining work
Assign each job to the machine with the least current work
Process jobs on each machine in order
methods.best_for: Reduces makespan, suitable for parallel processing
methods.limitations: Does not consider job priorities or machine availability

Knapsack.description: Knapsack Problem - select items with given weights and values to maximize value within a weight capacity

methods.name: Dynamic Programming
steps: Create a 2D table to store maximum values
Fill the table using iterative approach
Choose the maximum value from the table
methods.best_for: small to medium-sized problems
methods.limitations: high memory usage for large problems

methods.name: Greedy Algorithm
steps: Sort items by value-to-weight ratio
Select items with the highest ratio
Stop when the knapsack is full
methods.best_for: approximate solutions for large problems
methods.limitations: may not find the optimal solution

methods.name: Brute Force
steps: Generate all possible combinations of items
Calculate the total value and weight for each combination
Choose the combination with the maximum value within the weight capacity
methods.best_for: very small problems
methods.limitations: exponential time complexity

methods.name: Backtracking
steps: Start with an empty knapsack
Add items one by one and check the feasibility
Backtrack when the weight capacity is exceeded
methods.best_for: medium-sized problems with complex constraints
methods.limitations: high computational time for large problems

methods.name: Branch and Bound
steps: Create a tree with all possible combinations of items
Prune branches that exceed the weight capacity
Choose the branch with the maximum value
methods.best_for: large problems with complex constraints
methods.limitations: high computational time and memory usage

methods.name: Greedy Heuristic
steps: Sort items by value/weight ratio in descending order
Select items with highest ratio until capacity is reached
If fractional allowed, include partial items to fill remaining capacity
methods.best_for: fractional Knapsack problems or quick approximations
methods.limitations: does not guarantee optimal solutions for 0-1 Knapsack

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm
steps: Initialize a population of binary strings representing item selections
Evaluate fitness (e.g., total value) and enforce weight constraints
Apply crossover, mutation, and selection to evolve better solutions
methods.best_for: approximate solutions to large-scale Knapsack problems
methods.limitations: does not guarantee global optima and requires parameter tuning
